subject: Inference telemetry retention & subprocessor mapping for GreenHealth - security Q&A
messages:
From: Evan Lin <evan.lin@greenhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@greenhealth.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Security Qs: inference telemetry, retention, and subprocessors

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — GreenHealth is evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will process protected health identifiers (PHI) in anonymized form for clinical summarization. Our security team has a short set of questions we need answered before we can clear the pilot scope:

1) What telemetry about inference requests is logged (e.g., model_id, request headers, full prompts, token-level outputs, inference latency, requestor identity)?
2) How long are inference logs retained by default in your hosted environment? Can retention be configured per-customer?
3) Are raw prompts or generated outputs stored in plaintext on disk, and if so what redaction/pseudonymization options exist?
4) Which subprocessors may have access to inference telemetry or logs (cloud providers, observability tooling, logging pipelines)? Please include region locations where those subprocessors operate.
5) For private/dedicated deployments, what changes in retention/access model should we expect?

We'd appreciate a short technical diagram of the dataflow for inference logs and a roster of subprocessors that handle telemetry. If possible please return an initial answer by EOD PT tomorrow; procurement is coordinating a low-risk DPA annex for the pilot.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Lin

Marissa / Jordan / Naomi — draft answers below. I kept things succinct for the customer, and noted where pilot-specific config can be applied. I also attached an internal diagram (will publish a cleaned version for customer).

1) Logged fields (hosted API default)
- request metadata: timestamp, model_id, API key id (hashed), region
- request headers: subset (user-agent, x-request-id) — we do not persist auth headers or full cookies
- request payloads: prompts are stored in logs by default for 30 days; full prompt storage is used to support debugging, quality monitoring, and safety evaluations.
- model outputs: generated text is stored if customer opts into evaluation/feedback; otherwise outputs are ephemeral and not persisted beyond the ephemeral log window.
- operational telemetry: latency, token counts, error codes, and node-level traces (sampled)

Notes on sensitivity: we treat prompts as moderately sensitive by default. For customers processing PHI we recommend enabling token redaction and server-side pseudonymization prior to persistence.

2) Retention & per-customer config
- Default hosted retention for inference logs: 30 days for prompts and operational telemetry.
- Configurable retention options: customers can request shorter retention (down to 0 days) or extended retention for compliance; enterprise plans allow custom retention windows via the Console and an accompanying DPA annex.
- Retention exceptions: audit/export requests (e.g., legal hold) will be addressed via customer-requested exports and separate retention controls per contract.

3) Storage / redaction options
- Storage: logs are encrypted at rest using customer or Redwood-managed KMS keys (configurable). Prompt and output strings are stored in an encrypted object store; disk-level plaintext is not left unencrypted.
- Redaction options:
  * Server-side token redaction: Redwood can apply a configurable redaction pipeline that replaces tokens matching regex patterns (PII PHI templates) before persistence.
  * Client-side pseudonymization: we recommend customers perform deterministic pseudonymization or tokenization upstream of sending requests where possible.
  * Output controls: by default outputs are not persisted unless the customer opts into logging for analytics/evals.

4) Subprocessors with telemetry access (hosted) — initial roster
- AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2): compute (inference runtime), ephemeral object storage for logs (S3), and KMS (if Redwood-managed).
- GCP (europe-west4): optional region for EU customers using multi-region hosting (object storage + monitoring stack).
- Datadog: sampled observability traces and metrics (no full prompt persistence in Datadog; only aggregated telemetry).
- Sumo Logic / Log Aggregator (for audit logs): used for longer-term operational logs when configured; access restricted via RBAC and encryption-at-rest.
- PagerDuty (alerts): metadata only (alert payloads exclude full prompt text).

Regions: We will provide region-level subprocessor mappings in the attached CSV; key point — raw prompt persistence only occurs in the customer-hosted region(s) selected at provisioning and is not replicated across global regions unless explicitly enabled.

5) Dedicated / Private differences
- Dedicated: Inference runtime runs on a tenant-dedicated GPU pool. Logs remain in the tenant's dedicated storage; default retention can be configured in the account settings and contract. Subprocessor access is reduced (no multi-tenant log pipelines).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Customer-hosted storage and observability are the default. Redwood control plane can be configured to never persist prompts; telemetry can be forwarded to customer-managed SIEMs.

Attachments / Diagram: I attached an internal dataflow diagram (inference_dataflow_v1.png) and will produce a customer-facing version showing the minimal telemetry retained for the pilot. Naomi — attached roster in CSV will enumerate subprocessors + regions for procurement.

Action items for Marissa:
- Approve the customer-facing wording and I will reformat for Evan.
- Naomi: please attach the subprocessor CSV and add any missing partner entries.

Hi Evan — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise customer-facing summary and the initial dataflow diagram we discussed. Key points up front:

- Default hosted retention for inference prompts and operational telemetry is 30 days; retention is configurable per-customer and can be set to 0 days for the pilot.
- By default prompts are persisted (encrypted at rest) to support safety/ops; for PHI use cases we strongly recommend enabling server-side token redaction or running the pilot with client-side pseudonymization and 0-day retention.
- Subprocessor roster attached (subprocessor_roster_20260519.csv) lists cloud regions and partners; raw prompt persistence is limited to the provisioned region(s) unless you request cross-region replication.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments Redwood can ensure telemetry stays in tenant-dedicated storage or entirely in your VPC/on-prem stack.

Attachments included:
- inference_dataflow_v1.png (diagram showing request path, ephemeral caches, persistence store, and where redaction can be applied)
- subprocessor_roster_20260519.csv (initial roster with region fields)

Next steps: If you want we can provision a short proof-of-concept with 0-day retention and server-side redaction enabled; procurement can sign a pilot DPA annex that calls out retention = 0 and confirms subprocessors limited to the specified region. Happy to run a 30-minute technical call to walk the dataflow diagram.

Best,
